Synopsis:
The battle has ended with all the Smugglers dead. The Attacker Leader Farlin must have survived.

Cluster Contexts:
- WYR_SmugglersCave_AttackersLeader.json: The fight has just finished: the smugglers are dead and their leader, Farlin, survived and is congratulating the player while offering payment for the help. Farlin speaks like a Guild agent — he defends the Guild as a stabilizing force and frames the slain crew as agents of a dangerous upstart called the Stone Lord, a rumored (likely human) criminal tied to the Absolute cultists. The player’s lines show distrust of taking gratitude from criminals and press for coin and details about who they just killed, reflecting the Lower City’s tense, politicized underworld. Off‑screen, the city is brittle after recent terrors (mind‑flayer and cult activity), and Harpers and sympathetic tavernkeepers are quietly sheltering allies in cellar safe‑houses, so every scrap of information and payment matters.
- WYR_SmugglersCave_PreConflict.json: The scene opens on the brink of a pitched fight: Farlin’s Guild attackers are about to engage Caïros’s smugglers — the Stone Man’s forces — who are clearly overwhelming and were under‑estimated by the Guild. The attackers have already taken heavy losses to traps and an earlier ambush, so Farlin is desperate and tries to recruit the player on the spot, even invoking Nine‑Fingers to sell her cause. Caïros and his crew are openly hostile to everyone, and Minsc’s offhand interjection complicates the boasts about the “Stone Lord.” If the player helps Farlin, the attackers will fight as allies for the encounter (unless attacked); if the player refuses or stays out, the Guild force will likely be routed.

context: You arrive just after a bloody fight in which the smugglers are dead and Farlin — the surviving leader of the Guild attackers — is standing amid the corpses, congratulating you and offering payment. Farlin talks like a Guild agent: she defends the Guild as a stabilizing force, dismisses the slain as agents of a new criminal called the Stone Lord, and hints that the Stone Lord may be allied with Absolute cultists. The player is distrustful of taking gratitude from criminals and presses Farlin for coin and concrete details about who was killed. Off‑screen, the Lower City is brittle after recent mind‑flayer and cult terror, Harpers and sympathetic tavernkeepers are quietly sheltering allies, and every scrap of information or payment could make a real difference.
